exercise1.prompt: Convert "10" to an integer, multiply by 5, print the result
exercise1.hint: int("10") turns the text into the number 10. Multiplying the string by 5 instead would repeat it, giving 1010101010.

exercise2.prompt: Print "Hello, Alice! You are 25 years old."

cases.name: prints the full message
cases.expect_stdout: Hello, Alice! You are 25 years old.

hiddenCases.name: age holds the number 25, not the text

exercise2.hint: print() puts a space between comma-separated pieces, so watch where the spaces and punctuation land. Building the sentence with an f-string gives you exact control.

choices: A number if the user typed digits
questions.explain: input() hands back text without exception, which is why converting it with int() or float() is usually the next step.
Multiplying a string by an integer repeats it. This is the classic bug from forgetting to convert input().
int() raises ValueError when the text does not describe a number, which is a good thing: it fails loudly.

questions.prompt: How do you combine a name and an age in one message?
questions.explain: The f-string works with any types. Concatenating with + fails if age is a number, because you cannot add an int to a str.
